text:
Anya R.: Quick Q — we have an engineer who got an external offer and their manager asked whether we should do a counteroffer + immediate level bump vs a normal promo process. What are the official rules and ops steps?

Michael B.: manager here. Wanted to be clear on two things: 1) can we match an external offer outside of the promotion cadence, and 2) if we do a counteroffer, does that count as a 'promotion' for leveling records / calibration?

Lisa C.: short answer: we can do comp adjustments outside cadence for retention, but there are conditions. Longer: retention adjustments (counteroffers) are treated as comp changes, not automatic leveling changes. If the manager wants an actual level change (title/level), that requires evidence & calibration and should follow promo workflows.

Anya R.: ok — what's the paperwork/process difference? manager wants to move fast (candidate deadline end of week).

Lisa C.: process options: 
- Option A (fast comp match): Manager submits a retention adjustment request via the CompChange form with rationale + manager approval. Compensation team reviews (48–72h target). This changes salary and/or bonus target but does NOT alter level or job code. Effective date = payroll next cycle (see payroll cutoff).
- Option B (level + comp): Manager files a Promotion packet (evidence, peer feedback, new role expectations) -> goes to calibration. Calibration timelines are weekly; worst case 2–3 weeks. If approved, comp team does comp change with retro/PR as needed.

Michael B.: if we do Option A, do we still record the fact that it was tied to external offer? For audit/compliance.
extra:
Lisa C.: please include 'retention_reason' field in the CompChange form and attach the offer if manager confirms. We log it for audit but keep candidate confidentiality.

Sean D.: adding policy notes:
- We do not do title/level changes solely because someone got an external offer. Level changes must be justified by scope of work.
- Exception: if the manager can show immediate and persistent change in scope (e.g., taking on manager responsibilities), we can fast-track promotion evidence to the next calibration cycle.

Michael B.: payroll question: if we approve a comp match today and set effective date to next payroll, is there any way to make it retro to the offer acceptance date?

payroll-bot: Payroll cutoff reminder: to make a change effective on the upcoming payroll (runs on the 1st and 15th), submit changes by EOD 3 business days before payroll run. Retro pay requires additional paperwork (Retro Approval form) and may take 1 cycle to process. See: https://intranet/payroll/cutoffs

Lisa C.: retro pay is possible but reserved for cases where the comp change was mutually agreed earlier and we missed the cutoff. For counteroffers we usually set next payroll as effective date to avoid retro administrative overhead.

Anya R.: what about leveling records in the HRIS if we do Option A? Will the people ops/manager need to update job code later if a promotion happens?

Lisa C.: yes — if a later promotion is approved, comp records get updated and we issue any retro adjustments if promo effective date is before the comp match. We keep both records: the retention comp change and the promotion record.

Michael B.: what about equity refresh? Candidate is asking for an equity top-up as part of counteroffer — can we do that ad-hoc?

Sean D.: Equity ad-hocs are allowed but require exec approval for > $10k refresh value (or above band thresholds). Comp team will prepare a short memo for approvals. Timeline typically 3–5 business days.

Anya R.: thanks all. Action items for me: 1) manager to submit CompChange (retention) form + offer attachment, 2) comp team to review (48–72h), 3) payroll cutoff check and set effective date next payroll unless retro approved, 4) manager to start Promotion packet if they want level change.

Michael B.: noted. I'll have the manager submit the CompChange form today and ping Lisa. :thumbsup:

Lisa C.: I'll review as soon as I get it. If anyone needs the form link: https://intranet/hr/compchange

Anya R.: one last Q — if we do a retention comp and later deny a promotion, does that look weird for calibration? any guidance for managers on messaging to the IC?

Sean D.: guidance: be transparent — frame the retention adjust as temporary comp alignment to avoid losing the person while we evaluate role fit. If promotion not approved later, managers should document expectations and next-review timeline. We don't label the retention increase as a promotion when communicating.

Michael B.: copy. I'll coordinate manager message template with People Ops.

Anya R.: thanks everyone — closing the thread once comp change submitted.
